opening_message:
Ticket 1: Christopher Myers (employee ID E012) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E012.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Employee is a full-time Analyst requesting write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write (admin only if their role owns the system; Analyst does not own Source Code). Requested level is write, which is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E012 is a contractor with basic security training (HR note said full-time, but security records govern here). Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Requested write exceeds max, so grant read.
reason: The two notes conflict on employment type: HR lists E012 as full-time (which would allow write), while Security lists E012 as a contractor with basic security training and states security records govern. Under the contractor/basic-training classification, the maximum allowed access is read (write requires advanced training), so the requested write exceeds the maximum and must be reduced to read. Granting read is also safely within policy under the full-time interpretation, so read is the appropriate level.
